verdict.rationale: First-party self-hosting docs say Supermemory runs on your own hardware as a single self-contained binary, the same engine as the hosted platform, with local graph engine, embeddings and LLM. That covers running the memory layer on infrastructure you control. Nothing in the pack shows the self-hosted engine is built from open-source code, and the docs explicitly say there is no Docker; Docker was only an example, so that alone is not a gap. missing for 10: evidence the self-hosted engine is open-source/buildable from source, deployment and licensing details (e.g. whether the self-hosted option is plan-gated), independent hands-on corroboration of self-hosting.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the memory layer from open-source code (e.g. via Docker) on infrastructure I control

citations.quote: Supermemory runs on your own hardware. It's the same memory engine behind the hosted platform... as a single self-contained binary.
Local graph engine, local embeddings, local LLM. Your data never leaves the building.
No Docker. No database to provision. No config files. It boots in seconds with everything built in
